quarters.summary: Reliance Industries Ltd. reported a strong Q1 FY26-27 performance driven by oil prices, Jio, and Retail, despite macroeconomic challenges. The company is focusing on digital scale in Retail and maintaining operational resilience in Energy/O2C amid geopolitical volatility.

subsections.label: Consolidated performance and what drove it
points: Management framed the quarter as 'extraordinary' due to macro volatility, energy market shock, and supply chain dislocation.
Revenue increased by 25% YoY, driven by oil prices, Jio, and Retail.
EBITDA exceeded Rs. 54,000 Cr, a 10% increase.
PAT was approximately Rs. 23,200 Cr, a 6% increase.
Consumer businesses now constitute about 50% of the overall mix.
Capex was funded by cash profit, with net debt slightly lower QoQ at Rs. 1.23 lakh Cr.
Q1 capex was approximately Rs. 39,000 Cr.
Moody's upgraded RIL to Baa1 and S&P to A-.
Finance cost increased by 19% and depreciation by 9% due to Jio capitalization.

subsections.label: Oil-to-Chemicals (Refining & Marketing + Petrochem)
points: O2C revenue increased by 30% YoY; EBITDA increased by 17% to approximately Rs. 17,000 Cr.
Headline cracks/deltas overstate realizable economics due to shock costs.
RIL maintained 96-97% throughput despite logistics/availability crisis.
Middle East production fell by about 12 million bpd during this period.
RIL diversified crude sources and optimized trade/logistics.
Gas diversion to priority sectors forced more liquids, but RIL maximized gasifier throughput.
SAED drag and domestic under-recoveries were headwinds.
Planned turnaround lowered production meant for sale by 10%.
LPG production increased almost fourfold, impacting petchem feed slate.
High cracks but demand destruction outside India; India demand remained strong.

subsections.label: Petrochemicals
points: Quarter described as a roller coaster with crude changing 5-10% in a day.
Naphtha increased by 61% to $903/ton, with premiums and freight spikes.
Middle East PE supplies blocked, leading to PE delta surge.
Polyester deltas rose despite MEG delta declining.
Polymer demand was down 22%; polyester downstream hit by gas curtailment and labor disruption.
RIL's ethane advantage widened due to cheaper US associated gas.
Ethane logistics improved with new VLECs, increasing ethane availability.

subsections.label: Exploration & Production
points: Revenue increased by 3.2% YoY; EBITDA was almost flat/slightly lower.
KGD6 production and price realization were lower due to ceiling price.
CBM production crossed 1 million standard cubic meters of gas with better realizations.
Condensate realizations were high at approximately $107/bbl.
Rig arriving next month for KG basin exploration.
CBM continues 40-well program and multilaterals across both blocks.
KGD6 ceiling expected to rise to ~$9.9 in 2H.

subsections.label: Jio Platforms
points: Subscribers reached 533m; net add 35.2m in 12 months.
5G users reached 285m; home broadband 28.6m, with 14m AirFiber.
JPL revenue was Rs. 39,173 Cr, EBITDA Rs. 20,865 Cr, margin 53.3%.
Usage was 69.4 exabytes, with per-capita 43.7 GB/user/month.
ARPU was Rs. 215.6, with management denying underlying pressure.
Digital services revenue growth was ~20% YoY, outpacing connectivity.
Enterprise push is managed services-led, enabled by FWA.
78% FWA market share of net additions in India.
JPL PAT was Rs. 764 Cr despite strong EBITDA due to accounting shift.

subsections.label: Reliance Retail
points: Q1 revenue was approximately Rs. 90,000 Cr; underlying growth was 11.6%.
Customers increased by 11%; transactions by 46% vs revenue 12%.
Grocery digital orders increased by 116% YoY.
EBITDA was Rs. 6,309 Cr, slightly down YoY; margin was 7.9%.
Three-year roadmap focuses on digital commerce and hyperlocal delivery.
Quick commerce differentiation claims include transaction data and physical footprint leverage.
Grocery: 1,000+ hypermarkets; LFL +7%.
Electronics: LFL +16%; ResQ +27%.
Fashion: LFL +4%; Ajio Rush orders +136% QoQ.
RCPL revenue was Rs. 8,600 Cr, with rapid scale and supply-chain buildout.
RCPL claims #3 NARTD player in India, with plans for international expansion.

subsections.label: JioStar (Media)
points: Platform crossed 530m users; IPL reach 700m; CTV consumption +19%.
Tadka micro-content hub engaged 100m users in ~2 months.
Deep integration with OpenAI for conversational discovery.
JAMS in-house AI media studio launched AI-generated micro-content.
First in-app commerce integration with Swiggy.
Revenue was Rs. 10,946 Cr, with PBT also +14%.
Advertising hit by real-money gaming ban and US-Iran war impact.

subsections.label: Digital services and enterprise strategy
points: Digital services revenue growth was ~20% YoY, outpacing connectivity.
Enterprise push is managed services-led, bundling connectivity with security, managed Wi-Fi, ERP, analytics, and surveillance.
FWA leadership with 78% market share of net additions in India.
Patent position: only Indian tech innovator in WIPO PCT global top-20 with around 4,500 patents.

key_takeaways: RIL is explicitly trading near-term consumer margins for digital scale (Retail) and building new infrastructure moats (dark stores; data centers; AI/media tooling).

In Energy/O2C, management stresses realizable margin is constrained by procurement/logistics friction even when market cracks are extreme; nonetheless, RIL demonstrated operational resilience (near-full runs) and feedstock advantage (ethane-heavy slate).

Forward commentary is deliberately non-committal on near-term O2C earnings due to geopolitical volatility ('a lot of imponderables'), but management maintains confidence in structural positioning: 'structurally… we are in a good place right through.'

quarters.summary: Reliance Industries Ltd anticipates continued growth across its segments, with a focus on expanding its digital services, retail, and new energy initiatives, despite challenges in the oil and gas sector due to geopolitical tensions.

subsections.label: Group Performance
points: The first 11 months showed robust domestic activity and significant growth in telecom traffic on the 5G network.
Rupee depreciation was a concern, with an 11% decline for the year and 4% in March.
Revenue was up 10% for FY2025-26, with EBITDA up 13.5%, including a one-time gain from the sale of listed shares.
Consumer businesses contributed more than 55% of EBITDA.
JPL's PAT increased by 15% year-on-year, RRVL by 12%, and RIL by 24%.
Overall growth was 13%, with digital services showing strong growth at 18%.
Retail EBITDA growth was 8%, muted by the scale-up of hyperlocal e-commerce.
O2C grew by 10% despite challenges, and Oil and Gas faced production declines.
For the quarter, EBITDA growth was flat, with consumer segments (Jio and retail) up 14%.
Net debt remained controlled, with a net debt to EBITDA ratio of 0.64.

subsections.label: Jio Platforms
points: Jio Platforms ended the year with 524 million subscribers, adding 36.3 million during the year.
The 5G user base reached 268 million, with 77 million additions during the year.
Jio Platforms revenue for the year was Rs.1,46,085 Crores, up 14.6% year-on-year.
EBITDA was Rs.76,255 Crores, with a margin of 52%, showing a 190-basis point improvement.
Total data traffic increased to 241 Exabytes for the year, a 31% increase year-on-year.

subsections.label: Retail
points: Retail business achieved the highest ever revenues of Rs.98,000 Crores for the quarter.
EBITDA for the quarter was Rs.6,900 Crores, with a margin of 7.9%.
Hyperlocal commerce showed a 30% growth in average daily orders quarter-on-quarter.
The number of registered customers grew by 11% year-on-year, with transactions up 39%.
333 new stores were opened during the quarter, crossing 20,000 stores in total.
Grocery and fashion segments showed strong double-digit growth.
JioMart serves 1200+ cities with 3100 stores, offering two-hour delivery.

subsections.label: FMCG
points: FMCG business closed with a revenue of Rs.22,000 Crores in 2026, doubling from the previous year.
Campa brand delivered Rs.4700 Crores in revenue, becoming the fourth largest carbonated soft drink brand in India.
Independence brand delivered Rs.2600 Crores in revenue, becoming a promising and trusted brand.
The package drinking water business became the third largest in India.
International presence expanded to 40 countries.

subsections.label: Jio Platforms Technology Initiatives
points: Jio Platforms is implementing AI-first network optimizations, including energy optimization.
Network innovations include proprietary beam form cell design to improve coverage and capacity.
Distribution strategy involves working with OEMs to enhance user experience with new devices.
Customer experience improvements have led to Jio being rated as the best network by third-party reports.

subsections.label: JioStar Technology Initiatives
points: JioStar launched micro-content called Tadka, integrating horizontal and vertical content.
Deep product integration with OpenAI's ChatGPT transformed search functionality within the app.
In-app commerce integration with Swiggy allows users to order food during live events.

subsections.label: FMCG Manufacturing
points: FMCG is investing in manufacturing capabilities to become one of the largest manufacturers of cooldrinks in India.
The company is setting up integrated food parks to drive cost efficiencies and integrated operations.
FMCG has 12 plants across India and plans to expand further as the business grows.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and Economic Risks
points: Rupee depreciation is a concern, with an 11% decline for the year and 4% in March.
Supply shocks and their impact on industry and consumer confidence are major concerns.
Geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East, have affected oil supply and prices.
The introduction of SAED and its impact on the business is a risk that needs to be managed.

subsections.label: Future Outlook
points: Reliance Industries anticipates continued growth across its segments, with a focus on expanding digital services, retail, and new energy initiatives.
The company is optimistic about the resilience of demand for its products, despite geopolitical challenges.

guidance_ledger.statement: Expecting to ramp up the rate of connecting new homes significantly.
On track to complete 40 gigawatt hours of battery energy storage gigafactory at Jamnagar.
Scaling up to 20 gigawatt of solar PV module production completely vertically integrated.

Revenue has been led by digital services and retail, with EBITDA driven by strong O2C performance, 15% higher.
Balance sheet remains steady with no change in net debt number, leverage, etc., and businesses continue to deliver cash.
S&P changed the rating from BBB Plus to A Minus, focusing on higher earnings from less cyclical businesses.

subsections.label: Retail Performance
points: Retail business had the highest ever revenue at 97,600 Crores, up 8.1%.
EBITDA came in at 6,915 Crores with a margin of 8%.
Hyperlocal commerce is scaling up rapidly with 1.6 million orders and 360% Y-O-Y growth.

5G deployment helping win more customers with 65% share of 5G subscribers in India.

Daily essentials grew 1.5 times Y-O-Y, and the Independence brand crossed 1,500.
Energy portfolio reached 1,000 Crores in the quarter.

subsections.label: Jio Platforms Technology

World's largest fixed wireless operator with in-house developed solutions.
Home OS and tele OS offered to homes on connected devices, scaled to over 25 million homes.
Partnerships like JioHotstar and Google Gemini Pro enhancing customer offerings.

subsections.label: New Energy Manufacturing
points: Commissioning of the first fully integrated 10-gigawatt peak annual solar manufacturing gigafactory is on track.
Solar module manufacturing has reached a high yield of 94%-95%.
Battery manufacturing is progressing with a 40-gigawatt hour capacity, expanding to 100-gigawatt hour.
Construction at Kutch for solar power generation is in full swing, with significant land development completed.

points: Natural decline in KG D6 fields, efforts underway to augment production.
LNG prices have moved from $11 to $9.5, impacting overall realizations.
CBM productivity improved by almost three-and-a-half to four times in recent campaigns.

points: Strong growth expected in digital services and retail, driven by technology and innovation.
Continued focus on expanding new energy initiatives and integrated manufacturing capabilities.
Emphasis on maintaining strong cash generation and balance sheet stability.

quarters.summary: Infosys anticipates a challenging FY27 with revenue growth guidance of 1.5%-3.5% CC YoY, factoring in macroeconomic headwinds and strategic decisions to not pursue certain deals. The company remains focused on AI-driven growth and large deal momentum, despite expected margin pressures from wage hikes and AI investments.

subsections.label: Margins
points: Gains from currency and Project Maximus were reinvested in talent, AI, and sales and marketing.

subsections.label: Cash & Working Capital
points: DSO at 78, the lowest in 7 years.

subsections.label: Capital Return
points: Returned over $4 bn to shareholders in FY26.

subsections.label: Large Deals
points: Management emphasized that the large deal pipeline continues to remain strong.

subsections.label: Vertical/Geography Mix
points: Outperformance in Financial Services, Communications, Manufacturing, and Europe.

subsections.label: Financial Services
points: Driven by large-deal ramps, AI-led transformation, legacy modernization, and vendor consolidation.

subsections.label: EURS (Energy/Utilities/Resources/Services)
points: Demand is constructive, supported by a strong large deal pipeline.

subsections.label: Manufacturing
points: Cautious amid softer demand, particularly in automotive and parts of Europe.

subsections.label: Retail & Communications
points: Budgets are tightly controlled, with a focus on AI productivity.

subsections.label: AI Strategy
points: Infosys reiterated its AI thesis from Investor Day, focusing on a large addressable market for AI services across six areas.

subsections.label: Core Platforms
points: Topaz Fabric (AI) and Cobalt (cloud) are operational today.

subsections.label: AI Revenue Disclosure
points: Management confirmed AI contribution is above the prior disclosed 5.5%, but refused updated numbers.

subsections.label: Acquisitions/JV in Guidance
points: Stratus is included in guidance, while Optimum Healthcare and Versent JV are excluded pending regulatory approvals.

subsections.label: Geopolitics
points: Management acknowledged a change in economic environment after Middle East conflict escalation.

subsections.label: Competitive Intensity
points: Management acknowledged occasional competitor proposals outside the range of what models can deliver.

subsections.label: AI Security/Vulnerability
points: CEO described Mythos as exposing more vulnerabilities than one thought possible.

subsections.label: FY27 Outlook
points: Revenue guidance assumes a range of environmental conditions, with the lower end assuming higher deterioration and the upper end assuming improvement.

subsections.label: Seasonality View
points: H1 is expected to be stronger than H2, consistent with normal seasonality.

subsections.label: Guidance Drags
points: 0.75%-1% revenue reduction due to lower revenue from a large European manufacturing client.

guidance_ledger.statement: Revenue guidance is 1.5%–3.5% CC YoY.
Operating margin guidance is 20%–22%.

risk_register.note: Management acknowledged a change in economic environment after conflict escalation.
Management acknowledged occasional competitor proposals outside the range of what models can deliver.
CEO described Mythos as exposing more vulnerabilities than one thought possible.

risk_register.risk: Security breaches due to outdated systems
risk_register.note: Security breaches are increasing, necessitating modernization.
Tech debt must be addressed to leverage AI effectively.

The global environment remains uncertain, impacting client spending and decision cycles.
Majority of U.S. workforce does not require Infosys sponsorship for immigration.

themes.label: AI Deployment
themes.note: Infosys continues to focus on AI-driven growth with strategic partnerships and internal adoption.

themes.label: Large Deal Momentum
themes.note: Large deal pipeline remains strong, contributing significantly to revenue growth.

themes.label: Macroeconomic Uncertainty
themes.note: Guidance reflects potential macroeconomic headwinds and strategic decisions impacting revenue.

themes.label: Security and Legacy Systems
themes.note: AI security and vulnerability management are emerging as new service opportunities.

themes.label: Talent Acquisition
themes.note: Reinvestment in talent and AI skills remains a priority despite headcount reductions.

key_takeaways: Revenue growth for FY26 was 3.1% in constant currency, with Q4 growth at 4.1% YoY and -1.3% QoQ due to seasonality and slower decision making.
FY26 revenues crossed $20 billion, marking a significant scale milestone for Infosys.
Large deals for FY26 totaled $14.9–$15.0 billion, a 28% YoY increase, with 55% being net new.
Operating margin for FY26 was 21%, with Q4 at 20.9%, highlighting reinvestment in talent, AI, and sales and marketing.
Infosys returned over $4 billion to shareholders in FY26, with a proposed final dividend of INR 25, totaling INR 48 for the year.
AI strategy remains a key focus, with significant partnerships and internal adoption, though specific revenue contributions were not disclosed.
FY27 guidance includes a revenue growth range of 1.5%–3.5% CC YoY and an operating margin of 20%–22%, factoring in macroeconomic headwinds.

quarters.summary: Infosys is focusing on AI-driven transformation across various sectors, emphasizing modernization, talent transformation, and strategic partnerships to leverage AI opportunities.

subsections.label: Demand for AI Modernization

quarters.summary: Maruti Suzuki India Ltd expects over 10% volume growth in FY27, supported by capacity additions and demand, with a capex guidance of INR 14,000 crore for the year.

subsections.label: Sequential margin bridge (Q4 vs Q3)
points: Employee cost +100 bps (benefit) due to prior quarter one-time labor code provision.
Lower discounts +50 bps.
FX tailwind +30 bps.
Fixed cost absorption +50 bps from inventory accretion.
Commodities -80 bps.
New model expenses -60 bps.
Other expenses -20 bps (CSR/R&D seasonality/lumpiness).

subsections.label: Other income / mark-to-market mechanics
points: CFO quantified rate impact: ~46 bps blended benchmark move in the quarter drove ~INR 750 cr sequential hit (and INR 1,075 cr YoY hit).
Reversal is dynamic: 'As of yesterday, some amount of reversal has already happened. Roughly about 35% of this is already reversed.'
Credit quality remains conservative: 'more than 99.5% AAA-rated security.'

subsections.label: Industry context and demand shaping
points: H1 FY26: PV market -0.4% YoY, attributed to 'affordability pressures, particularly in the small car segment.'
H2 FY26: sharp rebound +16.7% YoY, 'led by the government's GST reform,' with recovery 'clearly led by the small car segment, particularly vehicles in the 18% GST bracket.'
Maruti’s domestic performance showed greater cyclicality than industry: Domestic sales -5.6% in H1, then +12.3% in H2, a 'swing of about 17.9%.'

subsections.label: Key strategic/product developments
points: Small car/18% GST segment regained momentum, with management noting that despite SUV-heavy market structure, 'the top-selling passenger vehicle… was the Dzire' (18% GST bracket).
Mid-SUV push strengthened via VICTORIS: 'Fastest model in mid-SUV to cross 50,000 cumulative sales.'
Won Indian Car of the Year, supporting brand momentum in a high-growth segment.

subsections.label: EV entry
points: Launched first BEV e VITARA: Positioned as 'first fully electric SUV developed on a fresh dedicated platform' for India and 'about 100 global markets.'
'Initial response has been quite encouraging,' but management said EV volumes are currently production constrained; near-term priority is '100% customer delight' (delivery experience, home chargers).
Management also flagged EVs as a structural tailwind to ASPs: 'EVs have to increase in the future. So that will help ASPs.'

subsections.label: Safety as a portfolio-wide commitment
points: '6 airbags as standard in almost all' lineup (volumes 'beyond 99%').
ESC and ABS+EBD standard across lineup.
Bharat NCAP: 5-star for all-new Dzire, VICTORIS, e VITARA, Invicto; Baleno 4-star.

subsections.label: Charging ecosystem buildout
points: Partnered with 13 charge point operators; target is 'over 1 lakh charging points across India by 2030' (with dealers/CPOs).

subsections.label: Inclusive mobility feature
points: Launched WagonR with swivel seat option to aid seniors/persons with disabilities, aligned to 'By Your Side' and UN SDG inequality reduction.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion and supply-side execution
points: Management framed recent GST reduction as 'transformative,' improving affordability and placing the sector on 'sustained long-term structural growth.'
To address demand and backlog, Maruti is accelerating capacity: Kharkhoda plant Phase 2 and Gujarat (Hansalpur) 4th line both to be operational within FY27.
Each adds 250,000 units/year, i.e., ~0.5 million units/year in one year, which management called 'virtually unheard of.'
Medium-term plan: increase capacity to 4 million units per annum.
Start-up costs: CFO expects no significant drag, as 'economies of scale should be able to broadly take care of the start-up cost,' assuming demand remains supportive.

key_figures.label: Export Share of India's Total PV Exports

subsections.label: Exports: scale leadership, but near-term uncertainty acknowledged
points: FY26 exports hit a record 447,000 units; Q4 exports also at record 137,215 units.
Maruti highlighted export dominance: the company 'alone contributed 49% share of India's total passenger vehicle exports.'

On FY27 exports, management explicitly avoided numeric guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty: 'If you can help me predict the war, I can predict the export number,' while aiming for 'at least the last year numbers.'

subsections.label: Geopolitical / supply-chain risk management and cost pressure posture
points: Management cited complex operating conditions: 'supply issues in rare earth metals,' West Asia conflict affecting 'energy, certain raw materials and logistics.'
Mitigation actions emphasized: Preventing production disruption (gas supply, alternate fuels, diversification).
Sourcing commodities at 'lowest possible cost,' supplier coordination, contingency planning.
Leveraging strong demand and utilization (pending orders support throughput).
View on persistence: pressures acknowledged but treated as manageable—'some cost headwinds do come and it's part of business'—with expectation they could ease when the crisis abates.

subsections.label: Outlook signals (FY27)
points: Volume growth ambition is company-specific: management indicated expectation of 'growth of over 10% this year' (Maruti), supported by capacity additions and demand.
FY27 capex: CFO guided ~INR 14,000 cr for the year.
Inventory (balance sheet) uptick explanation: mainly raw materials and WIP, plus goods in transit, positioned for 'ramping up the capacity in the coming 2 quarters,' not a finished-goods build.

key_takeaways: GST reform is re-accelerating small cars: strong evidence in order book (130k small-car pending orders) and buyer mix shift (first-time buyers up to 51%).
Supply is the binding constraint, not demand, near term—low dealer stock (12 days) + large unserved orders + aggressive capacity ramp.

Earnings volatility from treasury MTM is now a visible factor; investors should track interest-rate movements as they can swing 'other income' meaningfully despite robust AAA portfolio quality.

Strategic portfolio broadening: credible mid-SUV momentum (VICTORIS) plus first BEV (e VITARA) and charging partnerships position Maruti for mix/ASP uplift, though EV volumes remain capacity constrained in the near term.

quarters.summary: Bajaj Auto achieved record performance in Q1 FY27 despite operational disruptions, with strong growth in exports and electric vehicles. The company plans to expand capacity and focus on premium and electric segments.

subsections.label: Cost & Margin Management
points: CFO called Q1 'hyperinflationary' with commodity inflation rising to ~4.5% of revenue.
Specific increases cited: steel +10%, aluminum/platinum +~40%, rhodium +~40%, plus ABS, copper, nickel, natural rubber.
Inflation broadened into electronics, proprietary components, energy, logistics, labor.
Pricing offset 'nearly about half' of inflation with pricing in Apr & Jun.
Additional offsets: rupee depreciation and discretionary cost rationalization.
Despite cost shock, EBITDA margin 20.9% (+10 bps QoQ, +110 bps YoY).

subsections.label: Capital Allocation, Balance Sheet, and Subsidiaries
points: Standalone FCF ~₹2,300cr (≈80% of PAT); surplus cash ₹21,000cr at quarter-end.
Shareholder returns: CFO clarified July outflows include dividend + recently concluded buyback.
Total payout aligned to prior commitment of 100% payout of FY26 profit (~₹9,825cr).
Cash expected to dip post-July and rebuild toward ~₹15,000cr by FY-end.
Consolidation: Q1 consolidated includes first full quarter of Bajaj Mobility AG, reducing YoY comparability.
Consolidated revenue ₹21,689cr (+65% YoY); consolidated PAT ₹3,226cr (+46% YoY).
Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL/BACM): income ₹1,100cr+, PAT ₹227cr (>2x YoY); AUM ~₹20,000cr (+70% YoY); CAR 19%; ROE >25% (as of Jun 2026).

subsections.label: Forward View
points: Export run-rate ambition: move beyond '250,000 per month' from Q2 onward (vs ~200k/month only a few quarters earlier).
Domestic 2W: portfolio 'turnaround program' and heavy launch calendar.

key_figures.label: EV and Export Contribution to Domestic Revenue

subsections.label: Segment Mix Shift
points: Management highlighted exports and EV as standout: 'Taken together, our electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses delivered their largest ever quarter and are now at 30% of domestic revenues with double digit EBITDA percentage.'
EV profitability update (explicit): EV portfolio (2W+3W) remains 'double digit' EBITDA margin; Chetak moved from 'EBITDA neutral' to 'EBITDA positive.'
Exports: record volumes, broad-based share gains; aiming >250k/month.

subsections.label: Premium Exports
points: KTM exports from India recovered: +20% YoY; Triumph brand exports +40% YoY.

subsections.label: Domestic CV (3W incl. e‑rickshaws)
points: Industry (incl. e‑rickshaws) grew ~11% YoY; e‑autos doubled, now 44% of L5.
Bajaj delivered highest ever billings and retail; ICE share ~70%; EV leadership maintained.
L3/e‑rickshaw: new product 'RICI' in ~150 cities; company frames L3 as upgrade opportunity via quality/reliability/ownership experience.
Noted: L3 segment highly disorganized and largely lead-acid; regulatory pressure is limiting lead-acid permits; this is expected to drive lead-acid → Li-ion migration and upgrading.

subsections.label: Near-term Launch Blitz
points: Within ~6 weeks: complete 'exhaustive portfolio makeover' with:
'an absolutely new 150cc under the Pulsar brand'
'10 facelifts in the 160 to 400cc range' with 'class-leading features,' more electronics, and improved engine performance
'an absolutely new 125cc' Pulsar + upgrades

Later in FY27: introduce 'two new brands in the 125cc segment' (new nameplates, not Pulsar), with differentiated propositions; strategic aim includes upgrading 100cc customers into 125cc where innovation headroom and profitability are better.

subsections.label: Capacity Management
points: Capacity is now the binding constraint; plan to expand ~25% from 7mn to ~9mn units/year focused on EV 2W/3W, high-end motorcycles, and 3Ws.
Demand exceeds supply; capacity: currently ~50k/month, immediate unlock to ~60k/month via productivity/vendor actions; broader capacity expansion underway.

subsections.label: Africa
points: Industry grew ~50%; Bajaj grew ~2x that; retail 'doubled,' led by Boxer 125 Heavy Duty (upgrade).
Nigeria: pre-election institutional demand; Bajaj claims it captured disproportionate growth with ~60% retail market share; driven by Boxer equity and 'wide footprint of retail and service network.'

subsections.label: Latin America
points: Continued strong outperformance, especially Mexico (noted as 'amongst the top five markets of the world').
Drivers: success of NS / N250 models, 'well-organized supply chain in Mexico' and favorable tariffs (management cited 3%), plus distribution expansion (75 stores).
Region also positioned as a driver of 'corporate capital' (i.e., profitability/cash).

subsections.label: Asia
points: Muted due to Bangladesh/Nepal; focus shifted to defending share and dealer health.
Philippines: multiple launches + exclusive motorcycle stores to build the premium/personal motorcycling category.

subsections.label: Supply Disruptions Quantified
points: Multiple concurrent shocks: industrial fuel supply curtailment, West Asia logistics force majeure impacting alloys/polymers, labor shortages due to cost-of-living + elections.
Estimated lost production opportunity: ~10% of volume.

subsections.label: Industry Context (Demand Shape)
points: Domestic 2W registrations +14% YoY (Q1), slower than Q4 (+25%); growth led by EV scooters and 150–400cc motorcycles.
100cc & 125cc segments were 'flattish,' resulting in ~7% industry motorcycle growth.

Management interpretation: stress is concentrated 'down the pyramid'; higher-income cohorts remain stronger. They explicitly linked sentiment drag to West Asia crisis and household fuel pressures ('LPG availability into every kitchen').

subsections.label: Bajaj Strategy: De-emphasize 100cc on Profitability Grounds
points: Clear positioning: in 100cc, Bajaj will participate 'at our own terms,' and where 'growth and profitability… get into a conflict… we tend to favor profitability and are prepared to lose market share.'
Rationale: 100cc structurally shrinking (management cited industry mix decline from ~55% to mid‑40s over 5–7 years) and low 'degrees of freedom' for innovation.

subsections.label: Outlook and Strategic Priorities (FY27)
points: Management expects supply-chain disruptions to ease in Q2; rupee weakness seen as a buffer, but inflation/logistics remain key risks.
Explicit focus areas listed for FY27:
Domestic motorcycles: win in 125cc+ via portfolio makeover and new brands.
Exports: sustain share gains; push beyond 250k/month.
Premium (KTM/Triumph): accelerate via network expansion and niche category build (adventure/sport).
Electric: capture rapid growth in 2W & 3W; improve availability.
Capacity management to maximize availability.
Support KTMAG turnaround to 'normative level.'
Continue scaling and performance in BACL.

guidance_ledger.statement: Move beyond 250,000 per month from Q2 onward (vs ~200k/month only a few quarters earlier).
Win in 125cc+ via portfolio makeover and new brands.
Accelerate via network expansion and niche category build (adventure/sport).
Capture rapid growth in 2W & 3W; improve availability.
Expand ~25% from 7mn to ~9mn units/year focused on EV 2W/3W, high-end motorcycles, and 3Ws.
The 150cc plus segment should grow at twice the industry rate.
We expect to outpace industry growth in the 125cc plus segment and particularly in the 150cc plus segment and continue on the path of market share acquisition.
We expect to start to scale up Riki beginning quarter 1.
The industry should improve its growth rate by 6 to 8 percentage points.
We are taking steps to build three-wheeler capacity, particularly in the e-vehicle segment.
We will aim to maintain the leadership position here on.

risk_register.note: Management expects disruptions to ease in Q2, but inflation/logistics remain key risks.
Commodity inflation rose to ~4.5% of revenue, with specific increases in steel, aluminum, platinum, and rhodium.
West Asia logistics force majeure impacting alloys/polymers.
Noble metals, including rhodium, platinum and palladium are further heating up.
Inflation could diminish the purchasing power of customers, impacting growth.
Constraints in e-components and manufacturing capacity impacted EV segment.
Cost pressures across key commodities, including steel and noble metals.

themes.note: Exports hit a new high with broad-based share gains and record volumes.

themes.label: Electric vehicle growth
themes.note: EVs delivered their largest ever quarter, now at 30% of domestic revenues.

themes.label: Commodity cost pressures
themes.note: Commodity inflation rose to ~4.5% of revenue, impacting margins.

themes.label: Geopolitical risks
themes.note: West Asia logistics force majeure impacting alloys/polymers.

themes.label: Capacity expansion

key_takeaways: Management described Q1 as “the highest quarterly performance across all parameters” with 1.4mn units, ₹17,244cr revenue, ₹3,596cr EBITDA, ~₹3,000cr PAT and 20.9% EBITDA margin.
The quarter was operationally volatile: RM inflation, supply chain/logistics disruptions, and a ransomware attack.
Combined disruptions impaired availability by ~10–15%, “more so in exports, high-end bikes, and EVs.”

Management highlighted exports and EV as standout: “Taken together, our electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses delivered their largest ever quarter and are now at 30% of domestic revenues with double digit EBITDA percentage.”
Exports BU hit a new high of 732k units and ~USD 735m revenue (as stated), contributing ~40% of Bajaj Auto revenue.
Domestic 2W: portfolio “turnaround program” and heavy launch calendar.
Capacity is now the binding constraint; plan to expand ~25% from 7mn to ~9mn units/year focused on EV 2W/3W, high-end motorcycles, and 3Ws.
Management expects supply-chain disruptions to ease in Q2; rupee weakness seen as a buffer, but inflation/logistics remain key risks.

subsections.label: Quarterly Performance

Volumes grew 24%, translating into a 32% increase in revenues.

subsections.label: Annual Performance

Revenue followed through at nearly INR59,000 crores, up 17% year-on-year.
EBITDA closed the year at a new high of INR12,000 upwards crores, growing 19% year-on-year with margins at 20.5%.
Profit after tax came in at INR9,825 crores, nearly INR10,000 crores, with a growth of 21% year-on-year.

subsections.label: Export Demand
points: Exports business unit crossed the 6,00,000 units mark for the second consecutive quarter, clocking 25% growth year-on-year.
Latin America continues to outperform, delivering sustained growth for 11 consecutive quarters.
Asia recorded double-digit growth, particularly due to Sri Lanka, Philippines and Nepal.

subsections.label: Domestic Demand
points: Domestic motorcycles saw a growth of around 11% for the full year.
The 125cc plus segment grew faster than the 100cc segment.
The 150cc plus segment was the fastest growing.

subsections.label: Motorcycles
points: Pulsar brand delivered record export volume for the quarter.
KTM and Triumph brands delivered a record domestic performance in quarter 4 with combined volumes of nearly 43,000 units.
The N and NS series of Pulsar grew at over twice the rate of the industry in Q4.

subsections.label: Electric Vehicles
points: Chetak crossed the 1 lakh retail mark for the very first time in a single quarter.
Chetak's market share moved up to almost 23%, a gain of 170 basis points sequentially.
In FY26, Chetak crossed the 5-lakh unit mark at INR4,000 crores in revenue.

subsections.label: Commercial Vehicles
points: The commercial vehicle business crossed the 5-lakh unit mark for the full year.
The ICE franchise remains rock solid with a share in the CNG segment close to 90%.

subsections.label: Regional Performance
points: Latin America remains a key driver of export performance in terms of volume, revenue and EBITDA.
Brazil sales nearly 10,000 units during the quarter, supported by expanded manufacturing capacity.
Nigeria reached some stability in Q4 with volumes crossing 1 lakh units.

subsections.label: Logistics and Supply Chain
points: Supply chain difficulties in terms of the LPG shortage, manpower availability and outbound logistics to overseas markets have impaired availability to service demand by about 10% to 15%.
Despite disruptions, logistics in export have not lost any sale.

subsections.label: Commodity Inflation
points: The cost environment is seeing a potential rise during the quarter of about 3% to 5%, driven by the metal complex.
Significant inflation is now visible across almost the entire basket with not just noble metals, but also base metals like steel and aluminium.

subsections.label: Geopolitical Risks
points: There is a potential for further disruptions due to the geopolitical issues in the Middle East.

subsections.label: Outlook
points: We expect our growth tempo to actually continue in Q1 basis the strong competitive positions we enjoy in the key segments.
We are looking at moving the exports needle to 2,20,000 units per month this quarter, up from the 2,00,000 levels.
The 150cc plus segment and electric segments, which are the absolute epicentre of our focus, mitigate the overall softening of the demand.

guidance_ledger.statement: We are looking at moving the exports needle to 2,20,000 units per month this quarter, up from the 2,00,000 levels.
The motorcycle category from its rocking 20% growth in Q4 to we estimate 7% to 9% in the near term.
The 150cc plus segment should grow at twice the industry rate.
The electric category in both 3-wheelers and 2-wheelers will witness not just continuity of growth, but perhaps a further increase in growth.
We expect to outpace industry growth in the 125cc plus segment and particularly in the 150cc plus segment and continue on the path of market share acquisition.
We expect to start to scale up Riki beginning quarter 1.
The industry should improve its growth rate by 6 to 8 percentage points.
We are taking steps to build three-wheeler capacity, particularly in the e-vehicle segment.
We will aim to maintain the leadership position here on.

quarters.summary: Bajaj Auto Ltd expects continued growth momentum in exports and domestic markets, driven by product refreshes and strategic initiatives, despite commodity cost pressures.

Domestic revenues reached an all-time high during the quarter, driven by double-digit revenue growth across all businesses.
Export revenues grew double digit in 8 out of the last 9 quarters.
EBITDA margins expanded to 20.8%, up 30 basis points sequentially.
Profit after tax after a onetime adjustment stood at INR2,503 crores, rising 19% year-on-year.

subsections.label: Demand Drivers
points: The momentum was set by the GST rate cuts, which sustained itself beyond the festive period.
Domestic motorcycles saw growth post-GST rationalization, with the industry growing by about 15% in Q3.
The CV segment in exports grew at 56% this quarter.

subsections.label: Motorcycles
points: Domestic motorcycles saw growth post-GST rationalization, with the industry growing by about 15% in Q3.
The 125cc plus segment is growing at a faster rate, with the 150cc plus segment growing even faster.
Pulsar received the benefit of consumer behavior transitioning from cautious to optimistic.

subsections.label: Commercial Vehicles
points: The 3-wheeler category was positively impacted by the rationalization of GST.
The Electric segment continues to drive the 3-wheeler industry by growing at about 50% plus.
Bajaj Auto maintains a 70% plus market share in the ICE segment.

subsections.label: Pro-Biking
points: The Pro-Biking business delivered a record domestic performance with combined volumes of over 35,000 units.
KTM volumes were led by strong demand across the Adventure portfolio.
Triumph maintained a healthy momentum despite the GST rationalization.

key_figures.label: EV portfolio contribution to domestic revenues

subsections.label: Electric Vehicles

The EV business now delivers double-digit EBITDA margin while improving unit economics.
Chetak regained nearly 500 basis points of market share during the quarter.

subsections.label: Exports

Nigeria, the largest market, doubled sales in Q3 compared to Q2.

The focus will be on operational turnaround and putting the business back on track.

points: BACL delivered a class-leading performance with penetration scaling to 45% levels.

subsections.label: FY26 performance highlights
points: FY26 was the highest ever topline and bottom line for Hero MotoCorp, retaining leadership as the world's largest 2-wheeler manufacturer for 25 consecutive years.

subsections.label: Cash / working capital
points: CFO highlighted cash discipline with operating cash flow of ₹9,395 cr, driven by working capital improvements.

subsections.label: Shareholder returns
points: Final dividend of ₹75/share and total FY26 dividend of ₹185/share, the highest ever, with a payout ratio of over 70%.

subsections.label: Operational momentum
points: Growth segments delivering with healthier channels.
Management emphasized execution in segments where Hero had been relatively under-indexed, with early traction.

subsections.label: Retail vs dispatch
points: Retail performance outpaced dispatch growth, leading to lower channel inventory and healthier channel stock levels entering FY27.

subsections.label: Market share
points: Management claimed share gains across 100cc, 110cc, ICE & EV scooters, global business, and Harley range.
In Deluxe 125, share dipped in Q1 but then gained share quarter after quarter for the next three quarters.

subsections.label: Parts & accessories (PAM)
points: Management sees large headroom as Hero services only about 50% of parts demand; remaining demand goes to gray market or other spurious parts.

subsections.label: Technology and organization
points: Continued investments in EV plus flex-fuel / higher ethanol blends.
All EVs and premium products are connected with over 3 lakh connected 2-wheelers on Hero’s cloud.
Increasingly leveraging Gen AI for better customer conversion and shorter development cycle time.
Appointment of new CTO Sachin Agrawal to accelerate R&D transformation.

subsections.label: FY27 investment agenda and capacity expansion
points: FY27 capex commitment of ₹1,500 cr confirmed.
Destini capacity already up 50%.
Xoom capacity in process of doubling, expected this quarter.
Near-term EV capacity expansion to be 50% higher than last quarter within a month.
Second phase of EV capacity doubling before end of FY27.
New global parts center in South India with investment over ₹700 cr to double parts handling capacity.

subsections.label: Geographic focus
points: Latin America showing good traction, expanding to more countries.
Africa currently relatively small, but opening countries and planning launches.
Bangladesh is the #1 brand, operating in about 50% of the market, planning launches into remaining segments.
Sri Lanka re-entered last year, rapidly gaining share.

subsections.label: Strategic framing: what stays strong vs where Hero is leaning in
points: CEO highlighted core strengths to maintain: dominant entry/commuter motorcycles, unmatched distribution/service reach, and strong dealer/supplier trust.
Incremental emphasis areas include scooters, EV, other low-emission powertrains, technology/connectivity/AI, and exports.

subsections.label: Other disclosed investment/strategic moves: Euler stake
points: Hero clarified it is not investing ₹200 cr quarterly in Euler; it completed a ~₹200+ cr follow-on.
Euler stake now close to 37%.
This investment should take care of their funding requirement for the current fiscal.

subsections.label: Cost environment & margins
points: Commodity shock since March with mitigation but near-term pressure.
Macro headwinds from West Asia developments impacting commodity costs, metals, gas, plus labor cost increases.
Commodity inflation disclosure for Q4: ₹2,000–₹2,100 per unit increase; revenue/unit also up ~₹2,000, but margin % still fell because price recovers value not percent.
Management expects transitionary impact on margins in the short term.
April price hike of ~2% does not cover current inflation: BOM cost inflation is high single digits, while price was ~2% on revenue.
Mitigation levers include further calibrated price increases, accelerated LEAP savings, value engineering/BOM reduction, operating leverage, and postponing discretionary spends.

subsections.label: Exports: momentum and geographic priorities; near-term risks manageable
points: Management noted fuel price hikes in Bangladesh/Sri Lanka could hit demand short-term.
Global container/transport costs are up but have been priced and passing it on so far.

subsections.label: Regulatory items: ABS and EPR
points: Mandatory ABS: no development over the last few months.

EPR draft notification described as evolving; operationalization and pricing still under industry discussion; potential retrospective impact currently under discussion with no quantified impact provided.

subsections.label: Guidance stance
points: Reiterated medium-term margin guidance of 14%–16%, but avoided committing to a precise FY27 outcome due to volatility.

subsections.label: EV economics
points: EV losses acknowledged as still in the phase of building out the EV portfolio with ongoing R&D and capacity ramp.
CFO claimed EBITDA losses per unit is actually coming down in each quarter.
PLI approved for 3 products, covering ~60% of EV portfolio; target to reach ~90% coverage during the year.
PLI translates to 13% of revenue as the benefit and is a key lever toward EV self-sustainability.
Management declined to provide EV revenue and loss number on-call.

quarters.summary: Eicher Motors Ltd reported a landmark year with record revenue and unit sales, and announced a strategic JV with Volvo for vehicle financing. The company is expanding capacity and entering the electric vehicle market with a controlled approach.

subsections.label: Royal Enfield Demand
points: Management sees sustained structural demand with no structural correction.
Premium motorcycle segment is expanding, with RE contributing ~90,000+ units monthly.
April sales reported at ~1.04 lakh, a 57% YoY growth.

subsections.label: Royal Enfield Product Actions
points: FY26 upgrades/variants launched include Guerrilla 450 Apex, 2025 Hunter 350, Meteor 350, Goan Classic 350, Himalayan Mana Black.
Meteor 350 cumulative sales exceeded 6 lakh since 2020.
Himalayan 450 sales increased by 53% to over 38,000 globally.
Distribution innovation includes plans to make the 350 range more accessible via Flipkart and Amazon.

subsections.label: VECV Segment Performance
points: Eicher brand HD trucks sold 25,155 units with a market share improvement to 9.1%.
LMD trucks sold 46,195 units, with management claiming leadership in profitable growth.
New segment (SUV/small commercial EV platform) delivered 2,452 Pro X units, including 726 EVs.
Eicher buses sold 18,651 units; Volvo buses recorded 712 units.
Volvo trucks sold 1,712 units.
Exports increased by 33.9% to 6,933 units despite a challenging external environment.
Aftermarket spare parts sales grew by 13.9% to INR3,045.5 crores.

subsections.label: Electric Entry and Commercialization
points: Flying Flea positioned as a 'City Plus electric mobility brand'.
Flying Flea C6 launched in Bengaluru with a positive response.
Go-to-market strategy involves a controlled city-by-city approach.
C6 won the Red Dot Award pre-launch; media feedback was very positive.

subsections.label: Royal Enfield Capacity Expansion
points: Current declared capacity is ~1.4 million; additional '500 module per day' to increase run-rate to ~1.6 million plus by June/July.
Cheyyar brownfield expansion with INR958 crores capex to lift total annual capacity to ~2.0 million by Q2 of FY28.
Andhra Pradesh greenfield MoU signed for 261 acres to support future growth beyond 2.0 million, with a tentative execution window of 24 to 30 months.

subsections.label: Royal Enfield Market Strategy
points: Management reiterated focus on 'middleweight between 250cc to 750cc' and did not signal intent to go below 350cc near term.
Existing platform potential in 350/450/650 was noted.

subsections.label: Volvo JV for Captive Vehicle Financing
points: Eicher plans to set up a 50:50 JV with Volvo for financing, leasing, and other financial services.
Eicher's capital commitment is up to INR750 crores for a 50% stake in VFS India via fresh equity infusion.
VFS India has been operating for over 10 years with an AUM of INR1,806 crores and a net worth of ~INR500 crores.
The JV is designed as a captive financing arm for VECV, EML, and Volvo Group products in India.
Management emphasized controlled growth and underwriting discipline, with decisions based on risk profile.
With additional capital, leverage capacity could support scaling to ~INR9,000–10,000 crores AUM over ~5 years.

subsections.label: Margins, Commodity Inflation, and Pricing Actions
points: Q4 FY26 commodity impact was a ~90 bps margin headwind.
January price increase delivered ~70 bps; residual ~20 bps mitigated via cost reduction and mix/model price variance.
Q1/FY27 expected commodity headwind of ~3% to 3.5% on material cost level.
RE took a ~1.75% price increase in April; management implied roughly ~50% recovery of inflation via price.
VECV announced ~2% price increases effective 1 April, alongside ongoing value engineering and commodity optimization.

subsections.label: Industry and Demand Outlook
points: No formal numeric guidance for FY27 volumes/industry, but tone remained constructive.
RE: strong inquiry/booking rates; 'working on fulfilling the demand.'
VECV: 'traction… quite good,' but environment 'dynamic' with 'global uncertainties… supply chain volatility.'
Short-term disruptions due to elections-driven labor migration and LPG availability created ~2–3 weeks of disturbance.
Europe: 'market adjustment year' with industry degrowth and OBD2B pre-registered inventory overhang.
US: tariff-related uncertainty acknowledged but characterized as small exposure.
Brazil: elevated as strategic growth engine with ~71% growth and product awards.

guidance_ledger.statement: Cheyyar brownfield expansion targeted to lift total annual capacity to ~2.0 million by Q2 of FY28.
Management sees sustained structural demand with no structural correction.
Leverage capacity could support scaling to ~INR9,000–10,000 crores AUM over ~5 years.
Might have to increase capacity in Bhopal if industry continues to grow.
Hunter 350 is expected to gain traction during the festive season.

risk_register.note: Expected commodity headwind of ~3% to 3.5% on material cost level in Q1 FY27.

quarters.summary: Ashok Leyland achieved record performance in FY26 with all-time highs in CV volume, revenue, profit, and cash surplus, and plans to continue strategic investments in new products and technology.

subsections.label: Record Performance
points: Management called FY26 a 'milestone year' with all-time highs in CV volume, revenue, profit, and cash surplus; described as 'the best annual performance in Ashok Leyland’s history.'

subsections.label: Dividend
points: Board recommended a second interim dividend of INR 2.50/share.

subsections.label: Cash and Capex
points: Net cash INR 5,899 cr at FY-end, up >INR 1,650 cr YoY.
Management cautioned against Q3–Q4 comparison due to typical CV seasonality/working-capital timing.
Q4 capex INR 203 cr; FY26 INR 1,050 cr, focused on new products, future tech, alternate powertrains and EVs.
FY27 capex plan: INR 750–1,000 cr.

subsections.label: Industry Demand Backdrop
points: Q4 domestic MHCV industry +21.5% YoY; FY26 +12% YoY.
Growth attributed to 'GST 2.0 rate rationalization' reducing prices ~10% and triggering replacement given fleet aging 'at its all-time high.'

subsections.label: Volumes & Market Positioning
points: Ashok Leyland domestic MHCV FY26: 105,905 trucks (share 30.2%) and 20,840 buses (share 34.1%); overall domestic MHCV share 30.8%.
Continued leadership in MHCV buses.
Q4 domestic LCV 21,801 units (+23% YoY), outgrowing industry; Q4 VAHAN share 12.8% (+90 bps YoY).
FY26 LCV 74,322 units (+12% YoY); FY share 12.7% (+80 bps YoY) and 'highest ever annual volume recorded in LCV.'
FY26 exports hit historic high 18,082 units (+18.5%); Q4 exports 5,322 units, marginally down YoY due to international logistics issues in March.
Total CV volumes (incl. defense): 220,437 units, surpassing prior peak FY19: 197,366.

subsections.label: Non-Vehicle Revenue Streams
points: Aftermarket: Q4 domestic aftermarket revenue +11.2% YoY; FY26 +9.5%.
Power Solutions: FY26 revenue +16.4% YoY.
Defense: FY26 defense revenue up ~20% YoY; management highlighted strength of order book and tender win pipeline.
Revenue disclosure: defense INR 800 cr 'in the books up here', and INR 1,200 cr including subsidiaries.
Defense order book: 'already above INR 1,500 cr' to execute; typical execution spread 1–3 years; management expects to maintain ~20% growth trend for 2–3 years.
Revenue disclosures (FY26): Spares ~INR 3,800 cr; Power Solutions ~INR 1,400 cr; Exports revenue ~INR 3,200 cr.
Revenue disclosures (Q4): Spares INR 1,060 cr (vs INR 950 cr last year); Engines INR 425 cr (flat YoY); Exports INR 1,100 cr (vs INR 825 cr); Defense INR 275 cr (vs INR 170 cr).
Management: no dip expected near-term in non-vehicle revenue.

subsections.label: EV & Energy Ecosystem
points: Battery manufacturing: Groundbreaking for greenfield battery pack facility at Pillaipakkam (near Chennai); construction expected to start in 8–10 weeks; start of production targeted Q2 next year.
Battery business currently within Ashok Leyland (not a separate subsidiary).

Phased roadmap: Start with pack (captive + energy storage), then expand to non-captive automotive demand, then cell manufacturing in a third phase—explicitly paced to EV penetration ('dovetail… investments with the demand scenarios').
Switch Mobility India: Achieved net profitability in FY26; CFO cited PAT 'INR 100-plus cr.'
Delivered 1,530 e-buses (+238% YoY) and 1,600 e-LCVs (+56% YoY).
Claimed market leadership in electric buses and 2–4 ton e-LCVs.
Order book 1,600 units at year-end.
OHM Mobility (E-MaaS): Operational fleet 1,400+ e-buses; likely to need funding as it buys and operates buses for STUs.
PLI: Company still working to meet thresholds; update expected in 4–5 months.

subsections.label: Service Network
points: Added 100+ touch points each in MHCV and LCV; 45%+ additions in North/Northeast.
Total 2,104 touch points (MHCV 1,159, LCV 945).
International footprint: Network expanded to 4 new countries in the prior year.

subsections.label: Demand Outlook & Industry Landscape
points: Diesel price/availability: Management noted sentiment impact and localized diesel availability issues (rationing in some pockets), though government indicates no supply shortfall; described as 'manageable.'
Near-term trend: Q3/Q4 strong; April positive; May no significant slowdown in MHCV/LCV per management.
Visibility via customer plans: CEO emphasized fleet owners’ 12–18 month plans remain intact post diesel hike: 'people are not changing their plans right now.'

No formal FY27 industry growth guidance: CEO declined to 'hazard a guess,' but expects at minimum Q1 industry better than last year Q1 and any temporary softness could become pent-up demand due to strong fundamentals (replacement cycle, high fleet aging, improved TCO from GST cuts).

subsections.label: Segmental Call (MHCV)
points: GST initially boosted ICV more; created mix pressure (HD trucks more margin accretive).
Expect tipper + multi-axle as fastest-growing, plus 'trip trailer' (mining-linked).
Potential moderation in ICV and some long-haul tractor routes (non steel/cement/iron).
Channel mix: In heavy-duty trucks, retail ~55–60% and fleet balance; retail proportion higher in ICV/LCV.

subsections.label: Subsidiaries & Capital Allocation
points: Hinduja Leyland Finance (HLF): AUM ~INR 59,000 cr (+24% YoY); PAT INR 491 cr (+20%); asset quality: consolidated net NPA ~1.4%.
Hinduja Housing Finance (HHF): AUM ~INR 16,000 cr (+15%); PAT INR 387 cr (+4%); net NPA included in ~1.4% consolidated figure.
Reverse merger: HLF with NBL Ventures progressing; expected completion within this or next quarter.
Subsidiary investments: Q4 INR 371 cr (mainly loan repayment in 'off-tier books'); FY26 INR 387 cr.
CFO noted GBP 30m repaid out of GBP 80m loan at Optare plc / Switch UK.
Forward funding likely for OHM, HLF, HHF; Switch India 'comfortable' after profitability.

subsections.label: Margins, Pricing, and Cost Levers
points: Material cost ratio: Q4 71.4% of revenue (+80 bps YoY); FY26 also 71.4% (+10 bps).
Management nonetheless stated gross margin resilience via 'better price realizations, rigorous cost-saving efforts and… product and business mix.'
Pricing actions: Jan price increase ~1% supported Q4 realization.
Q1 FY27 price increase 1%–1.5%, with uncertainty on sustaining through the quarter.
Commodity pressure: Management flagged 'significant increase… predominantly steel' entering Q1; refused to quantify magnitude ('too early to give a range').
Mitigation toolkit: value engineering, e-sourcing, supplier negotiations, turnover discounts; plus broader OPEX scrutiny.
CFO: cross-functional teams reviewing 'each of the operating expense… head-wise individually' to drive reductions.

Operating leverage absence in Q4: CFO attributed to one-time provisioning for performance-related bonuses and commodity turbulence; acknowledged analyst observation that Q4 didn’t show typical leverage.
Other cost risks into FY27: potential inflation in transportation expense (fuel-linked), conversion costs, and FX (rupee weakening) impacting 'other expenditure.'
Industry pricing discipline: CEO expects discipline to strengthen; 'industry… should look at taking multiple price hikes during the year' given input inflation.

key_takeaways: Demand is being underwritten by replacement + GST-driven TCO reset, with management repeatedly emphasizing baseline resilience despite diesel noise and localized disruptions.

Near-term margin risk is real and concentrated in commodities (steel) plus fuel-linked opex; company response is measured price increases (1–1.5%) + intensified internal cost programs, but with explicit limits if commodities spike sharply.
Mix and product cycle are turning more favorable if mining/infra-led tippers and multi-axles accelerate and new high-HP products ramp—management expects visible share benefit from Q2.

EV strategy moved from 'investment' to 'execution' milestone with Switch India profitability and a tangible battery pack manufacturing timeline; cell manufacturing remains optional/phase-3 contingent on demand.
Capital deployment is flexible and need-based, with likely incremental support for financing and E-MaaS subsidiaries, while Switch India reduces funding burden due to profitability.

subsections.label: Product Development
points: Our product development pipeline is stronger than ever.

Our non-diesel portfolio is continuously expanding, with two models of light electric trucks, three models of MHCV electric trucks and several models and variants of electric buses already available commercially.
We have also forayed into other greener technologies such as CNG, LNG and even hydrogen.
Within the diesel range, we are preparing to soon launch a completely new range of heavy-duty trucks with power ratings of 320 and 360 horsepower.
These new trucks are built with next-level of heavy-duty aggregates, delivering unmatched reliability.

These products would be fitted with our most modern 6-cylinder engines, delivering highest peak torque in the respective segments, enabling our customer’s best-in-class turnaround time and therefore more earnings per month.
We are also working on improving the throughput of our R&D resources, which will help us reduce the time to market and respond quickly to the changing market and regulatory requirements.

subsections.label: Capacity Expansion
points: We are continuously augmenting our fully-built bus capacity to cater to the growing demand of fully-built buses.
Our newest and most modern bus plant at Lucknow shall be inaugurated soon.
After complete ramp-up of our AP and Lucknow plants, we shall reach bus body-building capacity of 20,000 numbers-plus per year from that of roughly 12,000 numbers at present.
As far as the capacity is concerned, our current capacity is close to 80,000 units on the light commercial vehicles.
We have already laid out a plan to increase this capacity to 110,000-120,000 units without much of an investment.
Mainly these are process changes and some small investments here or there, but largely leading through process changes and efficiency changes.
No more floor area expansion, no more new buildings, etc.

subsections.label: Geographical Expansion
points: We also continue to expand our domestic network.
We added 27 MHCV points and 26 LCV touchpoints during the quarter, with most of the additions happening in northeast and the central areas.
With these additions, total touchpoints are about to touch the milestone number of 2,000, that is 1,100 for MHCV and 876 for LCV.
Internationally as well, we are expanding our network in all our four home markets with SAARC, Africa, GCC and ASEAN.

subsections.label: Supply Chain Management
points: We have been able to keep our operating capital very lean and have brought it down by almost 50% on Y-o-Y basis.
We are running several projects on better cash management, cost management.
We believe there is still a lot of potential left even in inventory ratios, inventory turnover, receivables, there is a lot more juice that is left.

subsections.label: Market Strategy
points: Roughly 50% of the revenue comes from the non-truck businesses.
With buses, about 13%; light commercial vehicles, about 12%; spares, about 10% and exports, about 7%-8%.
The margins from these businesses are higher than the domestic truck margins.
The share of domestic truck business was 60% in FY '22, now it has moved to 51%.
Our break-even volume we have been able to reduce drastically.

quarters.summary: Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd achieved record revenues in FY26, with significant growth in emerging businesses and a strong order book providing future growth visibility. The company continues to focus on capacity expansion and strategic partnerships to drive growth.

subsections.label: FY26 headline performance and quality of earnings
points: Record scale: FY26 delivered the highest ever quarterly and annual revenues.
Profitability inflection in Q4 attributed to improving profitability in emerging businesses, particularly lighting and electronics and aerospace.
Margins held despite inflation due to operational excellence initiatives, cost optimization programs, and improving efficiencies across plants.

subsections.label: Balance sheet strengthening
points: Leverage ratio at an all-time low of 0.8x, reinforcing the stated policy of <2.5x and internal aspiration of <1.5x.

subsections.label: Order book, portfolio mix, and strategic roadmap (Vision 2030 / 3CX10 / D.E.M.A.L.)
points: All-time-high book business of USD 96 billion, providing strong visibility for future growth.
Diversified across PV, CV, off-highway, rolling stock, 2W, and geographies.
Management emphasized emerging markets rising in the mix due to growth and manufacturing ecosystems supporting exports under 'globally local'.

subsections.label: Consumer electronics (within Lighting & Electronics / emerging businesses)
points: FY26 revenues increased ~7.5x YoY; Q4 revenues +46% sequentially after the second facility went live in Q3.
Achieved Q4 production run-rate aligned to annual guidance of 14–16 million units.
Third facility (GF3) commissioning remains on track for Q3 FY27.
GF3 described as the group’s largest facility, a size of 33 football fields.

subsections.label: Aerospace (non-automotive adjacency with accelerating scale)
points: FY26 revenues +40% YoY; order book increased >20% to USD 1.6bn.
Won orders across metallic parts, subassemblies, and wire harness for business jets and rotary wing aircraft.
Two new India facilities expected to come up in Q1 FY27 to serve the existing USD 1.6bn backlog.

subsections.label: Wiring harness and broader automotive operations
points: Wiring harness division saw ~170 bps QoQ margin expansion despite copper inflation.
North America recovery optionality expected to support further improvement.

subsections.label: Capacity and ramp characteristics
points: Third facility (GF3) commissioning remains on track for Q3 FY27.
Management emphasized electronics ramps faster than auto: orders can move 'straight 0 to 100' once the season/program starts.

subsections.label: Capital allocation, capex pipeline, and shareholder returns
points: FY26 capex: INR 5,911 crore (~49% of EBITDA), allocated to growth, backward integration, and maintenance.
FY27 capex guidance: ~INR 6,000 crore ±10%, with 50% growth / 50% maintenance.
16 facilities under development globally, 13 scheduled to come on stream in FY27; all are in emerging markets.

subsections.label: Supply chain risk mitigation
points: 'Globally local manufacturing strategy' reduced dependence on long-distance supply chains.
Red Sea disruptions had minimal impact.
For customer-nominated components: 'back-to-back supply arrangements' to mitigate escalation.

subsections.label: Inorganic growth pipeline and transaction timelines
points: Atsumitec integration: FY26 was the full first year, progress pleased.
Completed acquisition of another Honda San asset.
Yutaka Giken acquisition on track to close by end of H1 FY27.
Nexans automotive harness business closing expected end of June, beginning of July.

subsections.label: Cost headwinds, pass-through mechanics, and operational resilience
points: Copper prices increased 16% sequentially in Q4, ~38% YoY.
Middle East tensions led to crude-linked inflation late in the quarter.
Polymer prices in Germany rose significantly post conflict escalation.
Raw materials have long-term pass-through arrangements with major customers; timing lag of 1–2 quarters acknowledged.
Energy/gas/freight and some overhead-type costs are a matter of negotiations, but management expressed confidence in recovery due to strong OEM relationships.

subsections.label: Vision 2030 framing
points: Target reiterated: USD 108bn gross revenues by 2030.
ROCE moderated to 16.1% due to capacity build; aspiration reiterated: 40% ROCE across businesses over time.

guidance_ledger.statement: Targeting 108 billion in gross revenues by 2030.

key_takeaways: This has been our best quarter ever across all financial metrics, and proud to report that we have for the first time crossed 1,200 Crore in quarterly revenue and 300 Crore in quarterly EBITDA.
China's restrictions on the supply of heavy rare earth magnets to India continues. In response, we have shifted to alternative motor designs that do not use heavy rare earth magnets.

Uncertainties around US tariffs persisted, during the quarter. However, on a positive note, the US administration has extended the tariff relief related to USMCA content for 5 years, to medium and heavy duty vehicles as well.
Our current RFQ pipeline is the strongest in the history of the company, and almost 3 times compared to the same time last year.
Our BEV revenue share continues to improve to 33% in the nine-month period. This was 30% in H1.
The share of our India business has increased to 55% in Q3. Even as consolidated margins continue to remain at the 25% mark.
Our net order book stands at ₹ 235 billion and the EV portion remains high at 71% of the order book.

subsections.label: Quarterly Performance
points: Consolidated revenues from operations for the quarter stood at INR 5,336 crores, representing a robust 18% year-on-year growth.
EBITDA grew by 14% year-on-year to INR 603 crores with healthy EBITDA margins of 11.3%.
Depreciation increased by INR 27 crores to INR 192 crores following the capitalization of strategic facilities.
Finance costs rose to INR 45 crores, a planned increase representing the higher borrowing required to fuel capex programs.
The share of profit from associates and joint venture for the quarter rose to INR 64 crores compared to INR 55 crores in the prior year.
Profit after tax attributable to shareholders grew by 22% to INR 326 crores compared to INR 266 crores in Q4 FY25.

subsections.label: Full Year Performance
points: Revenue from operations for the financial year ending March '26 stood at INR 19,589 crores, translating into a robust year-on-year growth of 17%.
Normalized EBITDA for the period grew by 16% to INR 2,182 crores, underscoring the operating strength of the business.
Normalized EBITDA margins for the period remained stable at 11.1%.
Profit after tax attributable to shareholders for FY26 stood at INR 1,197 crores.
On a normalized basis, excluding both prior period income and exceptional items, PAT is INR 1,166 crores, representing a strong year-on-year growth of 24% over INR 943 crores in FY25.

subsections.label: Debt and Cash Flow
points: Net debt as of 31st March stood at INR 2,179 crores compared to INR 2,091 crores as on March '25.
During FY26, the cash flow from operation amounted to INR 1,722 crores, while capital expenditures stood at INR 1,572 crores.
Despite incremental debt primarily driven by acquisition, the balance sheet remains strong with a net debt-to-equity ratio improving to 0.30 as of March '26 as against 0.34 as of March '25.

subsections.label: Returns and Dividends
points: ROCE of 19.2% and return of equity of 19.1% for FY26.
The Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 1.75 per share for shareholder approval.
When combined with interim dividend already distributed, the total dividend for FY26 reaches INR 2.65 per share or roughly INR 153 crores.

subsections.label: Automotive Industry Overview
points: The Indian industry has exited FY26 on an exceptionally strong footing with a decisive and pronounced rebound in the second half.
Production volumes in Q4 FY26 grew by 19% year-on-year, reaching approximately 9.3 million units.
For the full year, the total production reached an all-time high of approximately 34.7 million units, representing a robust 12% year-on-year growth.
Passenger vehicle exports reached a historic high of 0.91 million units in FY26, a 17.5% year-on-year expansion.
Electric PV registration surged by over 80% this year, with retail sales touching approximately 200,000 units.
e-2-wheeler registration crossed 1.4 million mark in FY26, growing 21% year-on-year.
3-wheeler exports for FY26 reached approximately 0.46 million units, a massive 50% year-on-year increase.

subsections.label: Switches
points: The switch system business recorded its highest ever quarterly revenues of INR 1,343 crores, reflecting a robust 17% year-on-year growth.
For FY26, the division reached INR 4,871 crores in revenue, growing 16% from INR 4,204 crores in FY25.
Growth during the quarter was primarily driven by the 2-wheeler switching business, which delivered over 26% year-on-year growth.
The 4-wheeler switching business, under Uno Mindarika, also continued to outperform industry growth.

subsections.label: Lighting
points: The lighting system business reported revenues of INR 1,154 crores, contributing around 22% to consolidated revenues and recording a healthy year-on-year growth of 13%.
On a full year basis, the business delivered revenue of INR 4,402 crores, registering a strong 14% year-on-year growth.

A key highlight during the quarter was the receipt of a significant new order for unserved models, with an annual peak value of approximately INR 450 crores for the supply of 2-wheeler lighting products.

subsections.label: Casting
points: The casting business revenues for the quarter reached INR 982 crores, reflecting a strong 14% year-on-year growth.
For the full year FY26, the business recorded revenues of INR 3,694 crores, marking a healthy 15% growth over previous year.
Growth during the quarter was largely driven by a ramp-up of recently commissioned capacities across key locations.

subsections.label: Seating
points: The seating system business reported revenues of INR 381 crores during the quarter, contributing approximately 7% to the consolidated revenues.
For the full year FY26, the business delivered revenues of INR 1,416 crores, reflecting a strong growth of 23%.
The quarter's performance was driven by a combination of increased share of business with both existing and new customers.

subsections.label: Green Mobility
points: The green mobility segment achieved a robust 25% year-on-year revenue growth in the quarter, reaching INR 423 crores.
For the full year FY26, the combined green mobility business recorded consolidated revenues of INR 1,405 crores, registering a steady 7% year-on-year growth.
The construction of the new greenfield facility for high-voltage EV powertrain components is progressing on schedule.

subsections.label: Other Products
points: The reconfigured other product portfolio reported revenues of INR 1,053 crores, registering a robust 25% year-on-year growth.
For the full year FY26, this product category reported consolidated revenues of INR 3,801 crores, up 26% year-on-year.
Construction of the sunroof manufacturing facility is progressing as planned with commissioning expected by end of FY27.

subsections.label: Capacity Expansion
points: The shifting cum expansion of the 4-wheeler switching facility at Farrukhnagar is progressing as per plan.
The construction of the new greenfield facility for high-voltage EV powertrain components is progressing on schedule, with Phase 1 commissioning planned for the second half of FY27.
The project involves a total estimated investment of INR 550 crores to be funded through a mix of debt and equity.
For FY27, a total capital expenditure of approximately INR 1,750 crores is planned, comprising of around INR 650 crores towards sustaining capex and around INR 1,100 crores towards growth capex.

subsections.label: Financial Highlights
points: Uno Minda delivered strong financial performance with highest ever quarterly revenues and profitability.
Consolidated revenue from operations for the quarter stood at INR 4,814 crores, a 13.4% year-on-year growth.
EBITDA for the period grew by around 14% to INR 552 crores, with margins improving to 11.5%.
Finance costs remained stable at INR 45 crores, while depreciation expenses increased to INR 173 crores.
Share of profit from associates and joint ventures rose to INR 63 crores, with significant contribution from the TG Uno Minda joint venture.
Profit after tax attributable to shareholders stood at INR 304 crores, reflecting a 24% year-on-year growth.
Consolidated revenues for H1 FY '26 were INR 9,303 crores, with normalized EBITDA growing by 15% to INR 1,026 crores.
Net debt as of 30 September was INR 2,362 crores, with cash flows from operations at INR 678 crores and capex at INR 728 crores.
ROCE was 19.6%, with capital employed including capex for land bank and CWIP.

subsections.label: Automotive Industry Overview
points: Indian automobile industry registered a year-on-year production volume growth of around 9%, with total production reaching approximately 8.9 million units.
Domestic market remained resilient with 6% growth, while export performance surged 26%.
Export rebound was fueled by recovering demand in key markets across Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East.

subsections.label: Passenger Vehicles (PV)
points: PV segment demonstrated a gradual recovery with production rising 4% year-on-year to 1.32 million units.
Growth was driven by export volumes, which grew 23%, while domestic sales declined by 1.5%.
Exports reached an all-time high of 2.42 lakh units, reflecting strong international demand for Indian-made passenger vehicles.
Electric passenger vehicles saw a 31% quarter-on-quarter and 139% year-on-year increase in sales, reaching approximately 50,000 units.

subsections.label: Two-Wheeler Segment
points: 2-wheeler segment recorded year-on-year growth of 11%, with total production reaching approximately 6.9 million units.
Scooters led the growth, rising 12% year-on-year, while motorcycles grew by 10%.
2-wheeler exports reached an all-time high of 1.3 million units, marking a 25% year-on-year increase.

subsections.label: Three-Wheeler Segment
points: 3-wheeler segment recorded robust 18% year-on-year growth, reaching production of 3.5 lakh units.
Exports hit a record, rising 51% year-on-year to 1.23 lakh units.

subsections.label: Commercial Vehicles (CV)
points: CV segment recorded year-on-year growth of around 11% with total production reaching approximately 2.63 lakh units.
Medium and heavy commercial vehicles posted a robust 7% growth, while LCV registered a 30% increase year-on-year.
Exports rose 22% year-on-year to 0.24 lakh units.

subsections.label: Electric Vehicles (EV)
points: EV sales increased 31% quarter-on-quarter and 139% year-on-year, reaching approximately 50,000 units.
EV penetration rate in Q2 FY '26 was around 5%, up from around 4% in Q1 FY '26.
e-2-wheeler penetration rate for Q2 FY '26 stood at 7.8%, up from 6.3% in Q1 FY '26.

subsections.label: Capacity Expansion
points: Depreciation expenses increased due to commissioning and capitalization of new facilities, including the 4-wheeler lighting plant at Khed City and capacity expansion at 2-wheeler alloy wheel facility in Supa.
The first phase of 4-alloy wheel facility at Kharkhoda with capacity of 60,000 wheels per month is now under commissioning.

subsections.label: Supply Chain Challenges
points: 2-wheeler switch exports were impacted by supply disruptions of rare earth magnets during the quarter.
The magnet situation has been somewhat getting normalized in the ongoing quarter.

subsections.label: Aftermarket & International Business
points: Aftermarket business reported revenues of INR 332 crores, contributing approximately 7% of consolidated revenues.
Combined revenue from aftermarket and SPD channel amounted to around INR 592 crores.
International business contributed approximately 9% of total revenue during the quarter.

subsections.label: Strategic Investments
points: Uno Minda continues to invest in building capacities in line with OEMs' expansion plans and auto industry's promising outlook.
10 expansion projects are currently under implementation across product lines with investment commitment of INR 2,356 crores.

subsections.label: Global Economic Environment
points: Global economy displayed resilience despite significant policy shifts following tariff increases by the United States.
IMF projects global growth at 3.2% in 2025 and 3.1% in 2026, below the pre-pandemic average of 3.7%.
Advanced economies are forecasted to grow around 1.6% in 2025 and 2026.
Emerging markets and developing economies projected to grow 4.2% in 2025 and 4% in 2026.

points: Indian automobile industry entered the second half of FY '26 on a strong footing, supported by festive momentum, stable macro conditions, and GST 2.0 reforms.
The outlook for the rest of FY '26 remains positive, supported by new model launches, improved financing conditions, and favorable policy environment.

subsections.label: Financial Overview
points: Uno Minda delivered strong financial performance in Q1 FY'26, driven by broad-based growth across multiple product segments.
